paragraphs.text: A workspace-first browser for DSH sessions
# DSH Workspace Browser
A pure client-side DSH plugin that adds a full-width workspace-first browser. Open the sidebar entry
to browse workspaces, inspect their sessions, and hand conversation navigation back to DSH.
## AI implementation disclosure
The bulk of this plugin's implementation, its refactors, and the related documentation were produced
by an AI coding agent; the requirements and product direction came from a human. AI authorship is n
ot a guarantee of quality, security, or compatibility — review the source, the tests, and the verifi
ed DSH version before relying on it.
## Features
- Workspace grid and detail view, with registry/name/recent-activity ordering and native workspace r

eordering.
- Workspace cards keep only pin, new session, and a "more" control on the card (icon butt
ons, one line); hide, rename, move up/down, and delete live in an overflow menu with keyboard, Escap

e, and outside-click handling.
- Add workspace from the panel through DSH's native directory chooser
; the selected existing host directory is registered through DSH's public workspace service. If nati
ve picking fails, retry or use the manual path/in-app browse fallback; repeat paths resolve to the e

xisting workspace.
- Optional "simplify native session tree": off by default; when on, a compact ent
ry replaces DSH's native workspace/session area. Its "Opened sessions" list records sessions only wh
en actually entered, groups them by current workspace, preserves manual-entry order, and persists lo
cally; removing a shortcut never closes or deletes the session. Long lists scroll inside the entry w
ith a persistent slim scrollbar and a bottom fade while more content is below. Turn it off in the pl

ugin panel's settings (or unload the plugin) to restore the native tree.
- Right-clicking a session
row in the compact tree, or pressing the menu key / Shift+F10 while it is focused, opens DSH's share
d session menu for that row: copy session ID, rename, pin/unpin, fork, and archive/restore. The host
owns these actions, so permissions, dialogs, and failure feedback stay native; the gesture captures

that row without opening it.
[该节后续省略]
## Install
The plugin is not published to npm. Releases ship as prebuilt tarballs attached to GitHub Releases;
installing one compiles nothing and runs no install scripts.
### From a release tarball (recommended)

1. Open a **published** release and copy its `.tgz` asset URL, for example
`https://github.com/FFFen

gMJL/dsh-workspace-browser/releases/download/v0.3.0/dsh-workspace-browser-0.3.0.tgz`.
Draft releases

expose no downloadable assets, so their URLs only resolve after publication.
2. Install it into the
profile that runs the Web UI:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DSH registers the new bundle in that profile as part of the install, so there is no manual `dsh.prof

ile.bundles` edit to make.
3. Restart that profile, then refresh the Web UI. The entry appears in th
e sidebar panel list.
DSH installs plugins from an npm name, a git address, or a tarball URL. This project uses the tarbal
l form on purpose: a release is already built, so users never need this repository's development dep
endencies or build-script approvals.
If the bundle is present but switched off, re-enable it in the plugin manager; reinstalling an exist
ing package does not toggle it back on.
Optional integrity check before installing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### From a local checkout (development)

1. Run `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` in the repository.
2. Run `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add

link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-workspace-browser`.
3. Restart the profile. A `link:` install references
your working tree and is not a distributable release.
### Compatibility
The verified targets are DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` and `0.2.1-rc.5`; those are the releases `dsh.compatibilit
y` in the manifest declares. The shared session context menu needs `0.2.2-rc.1`; on `0.2.1-rc.5` the
compact tree still renders and falls back to the browser's own context menu. Other versions have no
t been tested, and DSH's own compatibility check may require an explicit approval before loading an
unverified version. The plugin does not patch DSH host code. The `./client` export is a DSH module-l
oader entry, not a general-purpose ESM import surface.
The client bundle includes `pinyin-pro` 3.29.5 (MIT) for full-pinyin and initials indexing; its copy
right and license text are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
## Scope and known limitations

- Search matches catalog metadata only; it never searches conversation bodies.
- Grouping, ordering,
archive filter, subagent visibility, workspace pin/hide, the simplified-sidebar preference, and the
enhanced-picker preference persist under the plugin-owned versioned browser key `dsh-workspace-brow
ser.preferences.v1`; opened-session IDs have a separate key, `dsh-workspace-browser.opened-sessions.
v1`. Neither stores session titles, paths, or bodies. Same-origin tabs synchronize through local and
storage events, with an unavoidable narrow last-writer race because localStorage does not offer tra
nsactional read-modify-write; writes refused by the browser fall back to in-memory state. The prefer
ence schema remains unchanged; an old saved density field is ignored while every other preference is

preserved. Search, detail view, filter expansion, and scroll position remain temporary.
- Rename us
es the public `ctx.remote.session.rename` endpoint without rewriting session logs. Archiving a runni
ng session requires an in-page confirmation and then requests stop-and-archive through the native wo

rkspace service.
- Forking does not navigate automatically; the result notice offers an explicit ope

n action.
- Adding a workspace first calls DSH's public `uiWorkspace.pickDirectory()` native chooser
, then registers the selected path through `workspaces.create({ path })`. The chooser opens on the D
SH host display (not necessarily the remote browser's computer) and depends on the host's configured
picker backend and desktop environment. Cancellation has no effect. If picking fails, the plugin su
rfaces the error and offers retry plus manual path entry/in-app browsing via `uiWorkspace.listDirect
ory`; that browsing remains available only when supported by the Host composition. The path must be
an existing host directory; canonicalization, existence, permissions, and repeat-path reuse remain H
ost decisions. The plugin does not create directories or scan disk. Session deletion/migration and r

epair of old session ownership remain out of scope.
